title: Reading the open kernel module's headers: escapes, classes and controls
summary: Drake reads NVIDIA's open-module headers with three kinds of number in mind: escape codes say which operation (NV_ESC_RM_ALLOC, RM_CONTROL, RM_FREE), class numbers say what kind of object (each class has a header named after it, like cl2080.h for the subdevice), and control commands are CLASS 31:16, CATEGORY 13:8, INDEX 7:0 per ctrlxxxx.h. CUDA++ vendors exactly 67 of these headers, unchanged. I can walk you through splitting a control command in Omega and finding its class.
goal: Find the RM API in the open kernel module's headers and read escape codes, class numbers and control commands.
key_steps: Find the escapes in nv_escape.h and nv-ioctl-numbers.h.
Find the parameter structs in nvos.h.
Map a class number to its class/clXXXX.h header.
Split a control command into class, category and index.
Check the class part names the object you send it to.

example.code:
note Split RM control command numbers into the fields ctrlxxxx.h defines:
note CLASS 31:16, CATEGORY 13:8, INDEX 7:0. Bits 8..15 outside CATEGORY (14 and 15) must be 0.
note Input: decimal command numbers on stdin, one per line. Exit 0 all well formed,
note 7 a number with bits 14..15 set (not a command this layout can produce), 3 no input.
om2
global ob uchar 4096
global on ulong 1
global inb uchar 4096
global inn ulong 1
global inp ulong 1
text hx "0123456789abcdef"
fn putc c uchar to void
put ob get on 0 c
put on 0 add get on 0 1
end
fn puts s view uchar * to void
for i ulong len s
putc get s i
end
end
fn putdec v ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
n = ulong 0
x = v
while true bound 21
put d n uchar add rem x 10 48
n = add n 1
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
while gt n 0 bound 21
n = sub n 1
putc get d n
end
end
fn puthex v ulong w ulong to void
putc 48
putc 120
for i ulong w
s = mul sub sub w 1 i 4
putc get hx and shr v s 0xf
end
end
fn flush to void
w = write 1 ob 0 get on 0
put on 0 0
end
note Read all of stdin; every pass adds at least one byte to a 4096-byte buffer.
fn slurp to bool
while lt get inn 0 4096 bound 4097
k = read 0 inb get inn 0 sub 4096 get inn 0
if lt k 0
ret false
end
if eq k 0
ret true
end
put inn 0 add get inn 0 ulong k
end
ret false
end
note Next decimal number in the input; returns 2^64-1 when none is left.
fn nextnum to ulong
v = ulong 0
seen = false
while lt get inp 0 get inn 0 bound 4097
c = get inb get inp 0
put inp 0 add get inp 0 1
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 ulong sub c 48
seen = true
else
if seen
ret v
end
end
end
if seen
ret v
end
ret 18446744073709551615
end
text scmd "cmd "
text scls " class=0x"
text scat " category=0x"
text sidx " index=0x"
text sbad " REFUSED: bits 14..15 are set\n"
fn hexn v ulong n ulong to void
for i ulong n
putc get hx and shr v mul sub sub n 1 i 4 0xf
end
end
fn main to int
if not slurp
ret 3
end
seen = ulong 0
while true bound 65
c = nextnum
if eq c 18446744073709551615
break
end
seen = add seen 1
puts scmd
puthex c 8
if ne and c 0xc000 0
puts sbad
flush
ret 7
end
puts scls
hexn shr c 16 4
puts scat
hexn and shr c 8 0x3f 2
puts sidx
hexn and c 0xff 2
putc 10
end
flush
if eq seen 0
ret 3
end
ret 0
end

== 5. which object class does each command talk to? (class/cl<class>.h, if vendored)
0x0000: class/cl0000.h defines NV01_NULL_OBJECT NV01_ROOT 
0x0080: class/cl0080.h defines NV01_DEVICE_0 
0x2080: class/cl2080.h defines NV20_SUBDEVICE_0 
0xa06c: class/cla06c.h defines KEPLER_CHANNEL_GROUP_A

cmd 0x20805201 REFUSED: bits 14..15 are set
run rc=7

common_mistake: Copying magic numbers from a trace without the header behind them. Vendor the exact headers for one module version and derive every number from them, so it can be re-derived when the version changes.

evidence_note: EXERCISED on a Linux AArch64 host: ctrl.om compiled with the pinned omc and run on numbers grepped from the vendored headers, with a refused negative control (exit 7). Reads files only; says nothing about GPU behaviour.
